arguments.name: New Testament criteria establish reliable historical data
arguments.speaker: Gary Habermas
arguments.conclusion: The New Testament criteria (eyewitness, early, embarrassment, enemy attestation, Aramaic substrata) provide reliable historical data for Christianity.
premises: P1: The criteria are used freely by almost all historical Jesus scholars, including skeptics like Bart Ehrman.
P2: These criteria test whether texts are early, eyewitness, embarrassing, or attested by enemies.
P3: Embarrassing passages (e.g., Peter's denial, James's unbelief, Paul's persecution) would not be invented by Christians.
P4: Enemy attestation (e.g., hostile sources admitting Jesus's crucifixion) strengthens historical reliability.
P5: Aramaic substrata point to earlier strata before translation into Greek.

st1.quote: these two bodies of data, one are called the criteria, the New Testament criteria

st2.quote: Is the text written by an eyewitness? ... Is it early? ... What about embarrassment?

st3.quote: As Paul Meyer, he's retired now, but professor of ancient history, Western Michigan University, he says, "If an enemy of Julius Caesar says the guy's an idiot..."

st4.quote: So why would they say him if they're not true?

st6.quote: There's about a well, there's about a dozen key ones, but some some scholars find as many as 20 or 25.

st8.quote: Eyewitness early enemy attestation, embarrassment, Aramaic.

arguments.prior_art: John P. Meier, A Marginal Jew (criteria of historicity), 1991; E. P. Sanders, The Historical Figure of Jesus, 1993

or1.quote: Almost all the historical Jesus guys use these freely.
or1.why: This is the standard criteria-of-authenticity toolkit long used in historical Jesus research; Habermas restates it as a package.

or2.quote: As Paul Meyer, he's retired now, but professor of ancient history, Western Michigan University, he says...
or2.why: It adds a named ancient-historian illustration (Meyer) for enemy attestation, a minor new piece of support.

arguments.weakest_link: P3/P4 (embarrassment and enemy attestation) are asserted rather than shown to be reliable indicators of truth.
arguments.develop_next: Give a concrete case where embarrassment/enemy attestation criteria were validated against independent evidence.

arguments.name: Paul's seven undisputed epistles are authoritative
arguments.speaker: Gary Habermas
arguments.conclusion: Paul's seven undisputed epistles (Romans, 1-2 Corinthians, Galatians, Philippians, 1 Thessalonians, Philemon) are authoritative historical sources.
premises: P1: Critical scholars unanimously accept these seven as authentic.
P2: Critics consider Paul authoritative and a good source, even if not inspired.
P3: Paul was a trained scholar and first-rate philosopher (as even atheist Anthony Flew admitted).
P4: Paul would not lie or change the truth purposely.

st1.quote: of the 13 books that have Paul's name on it, they will grant you the use of seven of them.

st2.quote: they don't think Paul's inspired, but they think he's authoritative.

st3.quote: Anthony Flu would say Jesus is a first rate ethical philosopher and Paul is a first rate philosopher.

st4.quote: if he's wrong, he wouldn't he wouldn't lie to you purposely.

st6.quote: So yes, you can cite those seven books.

st8.quote: Critical scholars unanimously accept these seven as authentic... Paul was a trained scholar and first-rate philosopher

arguments.prior_art: The 'seven undisputed Pauline letters' consensus (e.g., Baur onward; standard in critical NT introductions such as Kümmel, Introduction to the New Testament, 1975)

or1.quote: they will grant you the use of seven of them.
or1.why: It simply restates the long-standing undisputed-Paulines consensus.

or2.quote: Anthony Flu would say Jesus is a first rate ethical philosopher and Paul is a first rate philosopher.
or2.why: Adds the Flew testimony as extra support.

arguments.weakest_link: P4 ('Paul would not lie') is a character assumption, not evidence.
arguments.develop_next: Show an independent test that Paul's self-reported material matches external evidence.

arguments.name: Early creeds are pre-Pauline and high Christology
arguments.speaker: Gary Habermas
arguments.conclusion: Early Christian creeds embedded in the New Testament are pre-Pauline and present a high Christology, showing Paul did not invent Christianity.
premises: P1: Creeds are early traditions Paul explicitly says he received (e.g., 1 Corinthians 15:3).
P2: These creeds predate the books containing them and are pre-Pauline (before Paul's conversion).
P3: About 80% of these creeds focus on the gospel facts: deity, death, and resurrection of Jesus.
P4: They present a high Christology, as Richard Bauckham says, 'The earliest Christology is the highest Christology.'
P5: Even skeptical scholars like Bart Ehrman date some high Christology texts to 2-3 years after the cross.

st1.quote: These are extremely early... since they're pre-Pauline, Paul didn't invent Christianity

st2.quote: Paul says, "I gave you that which I also received."

st3.quote: Bartman says, "We have several of these high christologology texts from two to three years after the cross."

st4.quote: These texts are they predate the books in which they're written.

st5.quote: Jimmy Dunn said, "Yeah, I don't think he's not as conservative as the other two, but he he said, "Yeah, I don't think Jesus makes it into the shama here."

st6.quote: It may not be immediately obvious to you what he's saying

st8.quote: Bartman says... two to three years after the cross... Richard Balkam says, 'The earliest Christologology is the highest christologology.'

arguments.prior_art: Richard Bauckham, Jesus and the God of Israel / 'earliest Christology is highest' thesis, 2008; Larry Hurtado, Lord Jesus Christ, 2003

or1.quote: Richard Balkam says, think about this phrase, one line... 'The earliest Christologology is the highest christologology.'
or1.why: Habermas is largely relaying Bauckham/Hurtado's early-high-Christology thesis; a variant presentation.

or2.quote: Bartman says, "We have several of these high christologology texts from two to three years after the cross."
or2.why: Adds Ehrman's dating as a hostile-witness data point.

arguments.weakest_link: P2/P4 (that creeds are pre-conversion and already 'highest' Christology) rests on contested dating.
arguments.develop_next: Provide the actual Greek/date-critical argument for one creed (e.g., 1 Cor 8:6) rather than name-dropping.

arguments.name: Six minimal facts are conceded by nearly all scholars
arguments.speaker: Gary Habermas
arguments.conclusion: Six minimal historical facts about Jesus are conceded by about 95% of critical scholars and provide strong evidence for the resurrection.
premises: P1: Jesus died by crucifixion.
P2: Jesus was buried.
P3: Jesus's disciples had real experiences they thought were appearances of the risen Jesus.
P4: The disciples were transformed and willing to die for their faith.
P5: The message was proclaimed at a very early date.
P6: Two skeptics (Paul and James) had experiences they believed were resurrection appearances.
P7: These facts are conceded by virtually all critical scholars, including skeptics like Bart Ehrman and James Crossley.

st1.quote: we're using only six facts to which about 95% of scholars agree.

st2.quote: Jesus died by crucifixion... he was buried... the disciples were transformed... This message is proclaimed at a very early date.

st3.quote: I have a longer version of this lecture that I use with grad students that of these six facts... the pieces of data number more than 100 evidences all by the year 100 AD

st4.quote: we're using only six facts to which about 95% of scholars agree.

st5.quote: Why did James Crossly say, "I'll grant all six and I'm just not in the faith." ... You're right. This person is exceptional, but you wrongly infer that I want to get married.

st6.quote: They give us the strongest evidences for the resurrection of Jesus.

st7.quote: If you take this approved list, you can refute you can give the major reputations of every naturalistic theory.

st8.quote: Bartman believes there's 15 independently attested sources for the crucifixion of Jesus within a 100 years... there's about six evidences that the man in the shroud is dead.

arguments.prior_art: Gary Habermas & Michael Licona, The Case for the Resurrection of Jesus, 2004 (minimal facts method); earlier in Habermas's 1970s-80s work

or1.quote: I started with a longer list about 12, and then I shortened it to a shorter list, which I called the minimal or core historical facts.
or1.why: This is Habermas's own signature minimal-facts argument, restated by him.

or2.quote: Casey and Crossley... both date the Gospel of Mark about 40 AD.
or2.why: Adds the Crossley dialogue and Casey/Crossley dating as fresh hostile support.

or4.quote: of these six facts... the pieces of data number more than 100 evidences all by the year 100 AD
or4.why: Adds a counting/aggregation structure (100+ evidences across 6 facts).

arguments.weakest_link: The 95% consensus figure (P7) is asserted without a survey citation.
arguments.develop_next: Cite an actual published survey establishing the ~95% concession rate.

arguments.name: Paul's Jerusalem visits confirm eyewitness testimony
arguments.speaker: Gary Habermas
arguments.conclusion: Paul's visits to Jerusalem to interview Peter and James provide close access to eyewitness testimony, confirming the gospel message.
premises: P1: Paul went to Jerusalem 3 years after his conversion and spent 15 days with Peter and James (Galatians 1:18).
P2: The Greek word 'historesai' indicates Paul was doing firsthand research/interviewing.
P3: Bart Ehrman calls this one of the two strongest arguments for the historicity of Jesus.
P4: 14 years later Paul returned and presented his gospel to the leaders, who 'added nothing' to it (Galatians 2:6).
P5: This shows the gospel message was consistent from the earliest eyewitnesses.

st1.quote: Where do we get closer to eyewitness testimony anywhere in the New Testament than right here?

st2.quote: He says 3 years later I went to Jerusalem... I spent 15 days with Peter and James, the brother of Jesus.

st3.quote: a number of non-eangelical studies on histo conclude that what Paul is doing there is doing firsthand research.

st4.quote: they added nothing to me... But the gospel message is same.

st6.quote: Probably the most important thing Paul brings to the table is he had 15 days with the eyewitnesses and he ascertained their experiences.

st8.quote: Bartman calls this one of the two strongest arguments for the historicity of Jesus... 15 sources for the crucifixion.

arguments.prior_art: Galatians-based chronologies (e.g., J. B. Lightfoot, Galatians, 1865); Ehrman's historicity argument, Did Jesus Exist?, 2012

or1.quote: The Greek word is hysteresi... from which we get our English word history.
or1.why: A variant on a known Galatians-1:18 lexeme argument.

or2.quote: Bartman calls this one of the two strongest arguments for the historicity of Jesus.
or2.why: Enlists Ehrman's own ranking as new support.

arguments.weakest_link: P2 (that historesai means 'interview/research') is contested and depends on later usage.
arguments.develop_next: Give the lexical study showing historesai means firsthand investigation in this period.

arguments.name: The empty tomb is well-evidenced though not universally conceded
arguments.speaker: Gary Habermas
arguments.conclusion: The empty tomb is probably the most evidenced fact for the resurrection, though only about 75% of scholars concede it.
premises: P1: The empty tomb has more evidence in its favor than any other fact.
P2: About 75% of scholars concede it, compared to 95% for the six minimal facts.
P3: Even if the burial was in a pit, the empty tomb argument still holds because the body would need to be raised.
P4: No critic has seriously held the 'stolen body' theory for over 200 years.

st1.quote: the empty tomb, by the way, is probably the most evidenced of the facts

st3.quote: If you robbed the grave and stole the body, can't be the disciples because they were willing to die for it.

st4.quote: anywhere he's buried it makes no difference. My point still holds.

st5.quote: Well, Don Crossson believes Mark bait up the empty tomb and they threw Jesus's body in a pit and the dogs got him. Okay, notice I didn't distinguish

st7.quote: no critic has said this for over 200 years.

st8.quote: If Jesus was going to raise from the dead, he would be raised from the dead in the guy's living room.

arguments.prior_art: William Lane Craig, Assessing the Empty Tomb / The Son Rises, 1981; Habermas & Licona, The Case for the Resurrection of Jesus, 2004

or1.quote: the empty tomb, by the way, is probably the most evidenced of the facts if I don't count it as one of my uh six
or1.why: A variant of the standard empty-tomb argument, here folded into the minimal-facts ranking.

or2.why: Adds a percentage estimate relative to the six facts.

arguments.weakest_link: P1 ('most evidenced fact') is asserted without displaying the evidence.
arguments.develop_next: List the specific lines of evidence for the empty tomb and their weight.
